items.title: A Sympathetic Plaintiff and Well-Crafted Defense Dominated Clancy Trial
items.author: Richard Fausset
items.content: <article>The defense lawyer for Lindsay Clancy showed empathy for his client in showcasing her mental health problems. That may have made all the difference.</article>

items.title: U.S. Strikes Three Iranian ‘Shadow Network’ Oil Tankers, Military Says
items.author: Yeganeh Torbati and Leily Nikounazar
items.content: <article>The U.S. military said it retaliated after Iran launched missiles at two warships. The strikes came days after the two sides exchanged some of their most intense fire in weeks.</article>

items.title: Putin Meets Witkoff and Kushner in Moscow to Discuss Ukraine War
items.author: Ivan Nechepurenko
items.content: <article>President Vladimir V. Putin ordered a pause in strikes on Ukraine’s capital, Kyiv, ahead of the meeting with President Trump’s envoys: his son-in-law Jared Kushner and the businessman Steve Witkoff.</article>

items.title: Will Lindsay Clancy Be Retried? The Decision Now Facing Prosecutor Timothy Cruz.
items.author: Jenna Russell and Remy Tumin
items.content: <article>After a mistrial, Timothy Cruz must decide whether to retry Lindsay Clancy on first-degree murder charges, downgrade the charges or drop the case.</article>

items.title: The Purest American Culture Lives on at Local Festivals
items.author: Nat Segebre
items.content: <article>Turning local traditions into public spectacle is a U.S. pastime.</article>

items.title: How Naomi Osaka Became the Fashion Queen of the Tennis Court
items.author: Vanessa Friedman
items.content: <article>At the U.S. Open she is playing a whole new style game.</article>

items.title: Putin Denies a Draft Is Coming, but Some Russian Men Are Taking No Chances
items.author: Ivan Nechepurenko
items.content: <article>As the fear of a possible mobilization becomes a fixture of daily life across Russia, many men are deciding whether to flee, hide or sit tight.</article>

items.title: What Will Happen to Lindsay Clancy in the Long Term?
items.author: Mark Arsenault and Christina Morales
items.content: <article>Even as a jury failed to reach a verdict in Lindsay Clancy’s murder trial, her future is unlikely to include freedom, at least for a long time. But Americans have been divided over the goal of her confinement.</article>

items.title: Is There Alien Debris on the Moon? Some Scientists Plan to Find Out.
items.author: Becky Ferreira
items.content: <article>Researchers want to explore the idea that microscopic particles shed by alien civilizations have accumulated on the lunar surface, making it an archive of extraterrestrial technology.</article>

items.title: In Red States, Law-and-Order Republicans Turn Against Flock Cameras
items.author: Jesus Jiménez and David Ovalle
items.content: <article>The governors of Texas and Florida have taken steps to curtail the use of license-plate readers, even as the police say they help with solving crime.</article>

items.title: Harlan Coben’s New Book Is a Tough-Talking Writing Guide
items.author: Elisabeth Egan
items.content: <article>Even a very successful thriller writer fights self-doubt. His new tough-talking writing guide doubles as a memoir that explains why, and how to beat it.</article>

items.title: Inside the D.O.J.’s Investigation of Fauci and Other Virus Scientists
items.author: Benjamin Mueller and Glenn Thrush
items.content: <article>As Dr. Anthony Fauci has faced public scrutiny from congressional Republicans, the D.O.J. has pursued a quieter and more expansive effort against a wider circle of researchers.</article>
